chapter: Los Angeles 1947-48, Rock Island and bebop in New York
title: Drugs to keep up with Monk, Chano Pozo, and recording 'Mysterioso' and 'Epistrophy'
summary: He used cocaine and alcohol to cope, bought from Chano Pozo, and recorded with Monk.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Yes, I had to, because if I listened to him I wouldn't know where I was, you know. I had to resort to everything. I bought Chano Pozo out of cocaine and marijuana, and I'd go to the liquor store and buy me a fifth of VO and a fifth of Seagram's VO, and a fifth of vodka, trying to neutralize the cocaine. And I couldn't get drunk, I couldn't get loaded or anything else, but I was resorting to this to try to get way spaced out to keep up with Monk, and I couldn't catch him. So --

Yeah. So I had occasion to record some bop music with Thelonius Monk, which two of them I remember. One was "Mysterioso", and the other one was "Epistrophy". And we had a vocal on it. He yood Pancho did a vocal on one of them. I forget what it was. But it was out of his key and Monk made him sing it anyway. And Pancho's throat was sore for a week.

Couldn't get him to sing a note. He hurt himself. But at any rate, down through the years Monk has come into being more of a piano player, to the point whereas you can recognize what he's playing, you know, the melodic line. I heard him play "Just a Gigolo" as a solo. He could do it, but in little spots he would put Monk in there. Tink-tink-tink, you know. He would go off kilter for a minute, but he would come back to the melody, you know. But then, when I was working with him, there was never any melody. So Monk was a composer, you know. "Around About Midnight", "Ruby My Dear", and some others to his credit, you know. I can't recall offhand, but I recall playing quite a few of them.
He and Dizzy are very tight friends. Right?
It must have been a joy being on the same bill.
